content.intro: Advanced object design is about collaboration and stable contracts. Interfaces, composition, dependency injection, namespaces, and autoloading help change or test parts independently. In this lesson, focus on final classes and methods; then compare it with preventing unintended inheritance. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use final classes, methods, and class design when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Final Classes, Methods, and Class Design
content_blocks.code:
<?php
final class Tax { public function amount(int $price): int { return intdiv($price, 10); } }
final class Checkout { public function __construct(private Tax $tax) {} public function total(int $price): int { return $price + $this->tax->amount($price); } }
echo (new Checkout(new Tax()))->total(100) . PHP_EOL;

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
